'''Izuhayao no Mikoto''' (いずはやおのみこと, historically spelled いづはやをのみこと) is a [[Shinto]] deity venerated in the [[Suwa Region]] of [[Nagano Prefecture]].

'''Izuhaya no Mikoto''' (出早雄命, historical spelling: いづはやをのみこと) is a [[Kunitsukami]] venerated in the folk faiths of [[Nagano Prefecture]].

== Name ==
The deity's name appears in various forms, including '''Izuhaya no Kami''' (いずはやのかみ), '''Izuhaya no Mikoto''' (いずはやのみこと), '''Izusokuo no Mikoto''' (いずそくおのみこと), '''Izusokuo no Mikoto''' (いずそくおのみこと), and simply '''Izuhayao''' (いずはやお). Early records, such as the [[Suwa Jinja Ryakuengi]] compiled in 1902,<ref name="ryakuengi">{{Cite book|和書|title=諏訪神社略縁起|editor=守矢実久|publisher=中村甚之助|year=1902}}</ref> and medieval texts like the [[Suwa Kamisha Monoimi Rei no Koto]] (1237 CE),<ref name="Takei">{{Cite journal|和書|author=Takei Masahiro|title=祭事を読む—諏訪上社物忌令之事—|journal=飯田市美術博物館研究紀要|volume=9|year=1999}}</ref> also describe the deity as '''Izuhaya''' or '''Izusoku'''.

The deity is also known by other names, such as '''Izuhayao no Kami''' (伊豆早雄命), '''Izuhaya no Kami''' (出早神), and '''Izuhayao no Mikoto''' (伊豆速男神). Historical texts like the [[Suwa Kamisha Monogui Rei no Koto]] (1237 CE) refer to him as '''Izudome Myōjin''' (出止明神).<ref name="Takei" />

== Overview ==
According to the [[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]], Izuhaya no Kami was granted [[Junior Fifth Rank|Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade]] in 860 CE and was later promoted to [[Junior Fifth Rank|Junior Fifth Rank, Upper Grade]] in 873 CE.<ref name="sandaijitsuroku">{{Cite web|title=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|url=http://www.j-texts.com/chuko/sandai.html|website=J-TEXTS|accessdate=2019-07-19}}</ref> He attained [[Senior Fifth Rank]] in 878 CE.<ref name="ryakuengi" />

In the [[Suwa Region]], Izuhaya no Mikoto is considered a son of [[Takeminakata]]. Local traditions regard him as the second son and a successor who governed the Suwa area.<ref>Miyasaka Kijū, ''Faith in Suwa Grand Shrine,'' 1938, p. 3.</ref>

== Overview ==
According to the [[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]], Izuhayao no Mikoto was granted successive titles: [[Junior Fifth Rank]] in 860 CE, promoted to Senior Fifth Rank in 873 CE, and later recognized as a deity associated with the pioneering of the [[Shinano Province]].<ref name="sandaijituroku">{{Cite web|和書|title=日本三代実録|website=J-TEXTS}}</ref> In later tradition, he is described as the second son of Takeminakata no Kami and Yasakatome no Kami and credited with assisting in the development of agriculture and land reclamation in Suwa and surrounding regions.<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=諏訪大社の信仰|author=宮坂喜十|year=1938}}</ref>

The deity has also been associated with the [[Mishaguji]] cult, which venerated numerous guardian deities of Suwa's forests and lands. His connection to fertility, land protection, and healing (especially wart removal) has ensured continued worship at local shrines.<ref name="Moriyakeifu">{{Cite book|和書|title=神長守矢氏系譜|editor=諏訪教育会|year=1938}}</ref>

== Lineage ==
[[File:Moriya Family Tree - 守矢氏系図.png|190px|thumbnail|center|The first five generations of the [[Moriya clan]] lineage (from [[Moreya|Moreya no Kami]] to [[Yasugami]]).]]

The genealogy of the [[Moriya clan]] describes Izuhaya no Mikoto as the spouse of [[Tamaru-hime]], daughter of [[Moreya|Moreya no Kami]].<ref name="Moriyakeifu" /> He is generally regarded as the progenitor of the [[Suwa clan]].<ref>Yonekawa Kazuhiko, ''Revised Suwa Genealogy,'' 1921.</ref>

Children attributed to Izuhaya no Mikoto include:<ref name="ryakuengi" />
* [[Yagata no Sukune no Kami]]
* [[Itsuhayahime-no-Mikoto]]
* [[Kusanoi-hime]]
* [[Kameba no Kami|Kamoha no Kami]]
* [[Wakagi-hime|Wakakihime-no-Kami]]

== Lineage ==
The deity's lineage is detailed in [[Moriyakeifu]]. Izuhayao no Mikoto is married to [[Tamatsuru Hime|Tamaru-hime]], and their children include:
* [[Yagata no Sukune no Kami]] (also known as [[Arrows of the Field]])
* [[Itsuhayahime-no-Mikoto]]
* [[Kamoha no Kami]]
* [[Wakaki-hime no Kami|Wakakihime-no-Kami]]
These descendants are linked to the [[Suwa clan]] and other prominent local lineages.<ref name="suwasikeizu">{{Cite book|和書|title=諏訪氏系図 正編|editor=延川和彦|year=1921}}</ref>

== Shrines ==
Izuhayao no Mikoto is enshrined in numerous locations:
* '''[[Izuhayao Shrine]]''' - A subordinate shrine of [[Suwa-taisha]], this is the primary location for worship.
* '''[[Izuhayao Koagi Shrine]]''' - Located in [[Okaya, Nagano|Okaya]], this shrine combines the traditions of multiple local shrines.
* '''[[Izuhayao Shrine (Ueda)]]''' - Situated in [[Ueda, Nagano|Ueda]], it was historically referred to as Izube Shrine.
* '''[[Izuhayao Shrine (Takamori)]]''' - Found in [[Takamori|Takamorimachi]], it venerates the deity as a guardian of regional agriculture.
* '''[[Minakami Shrine]]''' - Located atop [[Mount Minakami]] in [[Nagano (city)|Nagano City]], this site integrates elements of [[Kumano shrines|Kumano Three Shrines]] worship.

*
